questions: Compared with iteration 1 (y = 0.03), does progress on the oval and s-bend recover toward iteration 0 levels while line_loss_events stays near 1? If so, the shorter lead was the cause of the progress collapse.
If progress stays low, does the 16 mm footprint blur the centre signal, so that the controller sees a flatter, less informative error near zero offset?
What kp, ki and kd did you use for the 60 mm span, and did the span-related gain scaling (about 1.3 times kp) stop the steering oscillation from rising?
Do any max_error excursions still happen at the same bend locations on the s-bend and slalom, and do they start after a line-loss event or before it?

intent: Restore the y = 0.05 lead while keeping the 60 mm span and 16 mm footprints from iteration 1. This isolates whether the progress collapse in iteration 1 came from the shorter lead, so the span result can be read cleanly. Expected: line_loss_events about 1, oval progress back above 0.5, max_error still near 0.06 m.
learning: Iteration 1 changed span, footprint and lead together, so its progress collapse cannot be attributed to any one of them. Iteration 2 restores the lead only. Next step depends on the result: if the lead explains the collapse, keep the 60 mm span and tune the controller; if not, test footprint size. max_error sits at 0.063 to 0.065 m on every track in both iterations, so it does not respond to span or lead alone. Turn rate, through wheel_track or mass, is the untested lever for that.
rationale: Iteration 1 changed three things at once: span (40 to 60 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), and lead (y 0.05 to 0.03). Compared with iteration 0, line_loss_events fell from 1.0 to 1.9 per run to 1.0 on every track, and steering_oscillation fell on the oval and s-bend. Progress, however, collapsed. Oval progress fell from 0.664 to 0.273, the oval finish rate went from 0.05 to 0.00, and the mean score dropped from 159.7 to 64.6. max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.065 m on every track, still just over the 0.06 m limit. So the wider sensing span solved the line-loss problem but did not solve the off-track excursions. The excursions are transient turn-induced departures, not tape loss. The score collapse is most plausibly caused by the shorter lead (y 0.05 to 0.03): the robot reacts later on bends, so it has less time to recover and makes less progress before it leaves the track. The span and footprint change is confounded with the lead change, so I cannot yet say which one caused the progress loss. This iteration isolates the lead. I keep the 60 mm span and 16 mm footprint, which gave the lower line-loss count, and return the lead to y = 0.05, the position that gave the best progress in iteration 0. If progress recovers while line_loss_events stays near 1, the lead was the cause and the span is kept. If progress stays low, the wider 16 mm footprint is blurring the centre signal, and the next step is either a 12 mm footprint with the 60 mm span or a 0.08 m span with 8 mm sensors. Body, wheel and mass stay the same, so the test isolates sensing geometry. Expected result: line_loss_events near 1, progress back above 0.5 on the oval, and max_error still near 0.06 m. The Integrator's controller is the main variable outside this geometry, so their gain changes will be reported in feedback.
